How common each taxon of a key is, from GBIF occurrence records

Source: R/quality.R
occurrenceWeights.Rd

Counts the occurrence records GBIF holds for each result of a key, optionally within a country or region. The counts can be given to keyQuality() or summary() as weights, to see how many steps the key takes for the taxa people actually meet.

Usage

occurrenceWeights(
  key,
  region = NULL,
  source = "gbif",
  fetch = qualGbifFetch,
  kingdom = NULL
)

Arguments

key

A dimoose key.

region

Where to count: NULL for the whole world, a two-letter ISO country code ("US"), or a GADM id for a country, state or county ("USA.27_1" is Montana). Anything else is an error. GBIF answers 0 for a GADM id it does not have, so when no taxon has a record in the region a warning asks to check it.

source

Where the counts come from; only "gbif" for now.

fetch

The function that asks GBIF: called as fetch(url, query) with a named list of query parameters, it returns the parsed JSON answer as a list. Replace it to use cached answers or to test without a connection.

kingdom

Optional kingdom ("Plantae", "Animalia", ...), which helps GBIF tell apart names that are used in more than one kingdom.

Value

A numeric vector of record counts named by the key's results (as in its Taxon column), NA for results that have no scientific name, that GBIF does not know or cannot tell apart, or whose request failed (each with a warning).

Details

A result written as "Common name (Genus species)" is looked up by the name in parentheses; other results by the result itself when it looks like a scientific name, which includes genera and families ("Salix", "Salix sp." and "Salix spp." all count the genus) and names followed by their author ("Puma concolor (Linnaeus, 1771)"). A result that lists several taxa the key does not separate, written "A / B" as keyFromRpart() and keyFromMatrix() write them, gets the sum of their counts. Each name is matched to the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, and the records of the name GBIF accepts for it are counted, so a synonym gets the count of its accepted name. This makes two requests to GBIF per name, one name at a time; after three failed requests in a row the rest are not tried.

A name that GBIF knows in more than one kingdom ("Morus" is a mulberry and a gannet) is not counted unless kingdom says which is meant.

Occurrence counts measure how often a taxon is recorded, which follows how conspicuous and how popular with observers it is as well as how common it is. A taxon with no records gets a weight of 0 and so does not count towards the expected steps at all.

See also

keyQuality(), checkNames()

Examples

# canned answers in place of GBIF, to show the shape of `fetch`
counts <- c("Acer negundo" = 61000, "Fraxinus pennsylvanica" = 48000)
canned <- function(url, query) {
  if (grepl("species/match", url)) {
    list(usageKey = match(query$name, names(counts)), matchType = "EXACT")
  } else {
    list(count = unname(counts[query$taxonKey]))
  }
}
leads <- data.frame(
  Statement = "1", Choice = c("a", "b"), Character = c("Leaflets 3.", "Leaflets 5 to 7."),
  Next = "-", Taxon = c("Box elder (Acer negundo)", "Green ash (Fraxinus pennsylvanica)")
)
occurrenceWeights(keyFromLeads(leads), fetch = canned)
#>           Box elder (Acer negundo) Green ash (Fraxinus pennsylvanica) 
#>                              61000                              48000 
# \donttest{
k <- montanaKey()
w <- occurrenceWeights(k, region = "USA.27_1", kingdom = "Plantae")
w
#>                     Box elder (Acer negundo) 
#>                                          397 
#>           Green ash (Fraxinus pennsylvanica) 
#>                                          114 
#>          Rocky Mountain maple (Acer glabrum) 
#>                                         1194 
#>                 Bur oak (Quercus macrocarpa) 
#>                                           14 
#>        Peachleaf willow (Salix amygdaloides) 
#>                                          108 
#> Narrowleaf cottonwood (Populus angustifolia) 
#>                                          127 
#>          Quaking aspen (Populus tremuloides) 
#>                                          929 
#>        Plains cottonwood (Populus deltoides) 
#>                                          203 
#>       Black cottonwood (Populus trichocarpa) 
#>                                          247 
#>              Paper birch (Betula papyrifera) 
#>                                          140 
#>            Water birch (Betula occidentalis) 
#>                                          177 
summary(k, weights = w)
#>                                          title couplets leads taxa depth
#> 1 Key to the native broadleaf trees of Montana       10    20   11     7
#>   problems meanLeadSteps meanTaxonSteps expectedSteps    bound efficiency
#> 1        0      4.636364       4.636364      4.142466 2.826027   0.682209
# }
